guide.title: Quick start
guide.description: Follow these 4 steps in order. This page now recommends the guided setup and update scripts first, while keeping the detailed manual OpenClaw CLI flow as a fallback.
guide.intro: MindAtlas owns the capability catalog, knowledge data, and execution runtime. OpenClaw owns the chat entry, tool registration, and conversation orchestration. After installation, the plugin also ships 5 MindAtlas skills: overview, dispatcher, auto-capture, retrieval, and summary. `mindatlas-overview` is the main router, `mindatlas-dispatcher` is the dynamic fallback, and the actual callable tools still come from the live MindAtlas capability catalog. In practice, the agent should route from the session-visible `mindatlas_*` tool surface first, not from an imaginary in-session catalog tool. Follow the sequence on this page from top to bottom: generate the secret, expose catalog items, run the guided plugin script on the OpenClaw host, then verify one live call from a fresh session.

plugin.title: Install and configure the plugin on the OpenClaw host
plugin.description: Prefer one guided script below. It will collect or reuse plugin config, clean old MindAtlas remnants, sync shipped skills, and restart the Gateway for you.
plugin.hostHint: Run every command in this step on the OpenClaw Gateway host. This page cannot execute those commands for you.

details.install: Install the plugin from the MindAtlas repository on the same machine that runs OpenClaw. If OpenClaw runs on another server, copy the `integrations/openclaw-mindatlas` folder there first. The guided scripts handle plugin install or reinstall, plugin config writes, MindAtlas-only legacy cleanup, conflicting skill backup, `configure:skills`, and `openclaw gateway restart`. The lower-level `configure:skills` command still only wires the shipped skills directory into `skills.load.extraDirs` and prints warnings by itself.
details.baseUrl: Set `plugins.entries.openclaw-mindatlas.config.baseUrl` to the MindAtlas backend or reverse-proxy origin that the OpenClaw host can really reach, then paste the bearer secret generated on this page into `integrationSecret`. The shipped skills guide routing, but the actual exposed tools still depend on the session-visible MindAtlas capability surface.
details.refresh: Catalog availability changes can be picked up by the plugin refresh cycle. If a tool name, exported title, exported description, or input schema changes, active sessions will not hot-refresh. Start a new session or reload the OpenClaw Gateway or plugin. If a session shows no `mindatlas_*` tools, the agent should say MindAtlas is not exposed in that session instead of silently falling back to generic memory.

verify.title: Verify from a fresh OpenClaw session
verify.description: The guided scripts already restart the Gateway. This step is just to open a brand-new OpenClaw session and confirm the session no longer says MindAtlas tools are missing.

guide.installTitle: Manual install fallback on the OpenClaw host
guide.installDescription: These manual commands are only needed when you cannot use the guided scripts. The plugin package lives in this MindAtlas repository, and installation also brings in the 5 shipped MindAtlas skills. Plugin install registers the package, `configure:skills` wires the shipped skills into the official skills loader path, and a new session is still required before the refreshed skill and tool surface appears in prompts.

setup.title: First-time install script
setup.description: Use this on the OpenClaw host for the first install. The script always prompts for `baseUrl`, `integrationSecret`, `requestTimeoutMs`, and `catalogRefreshTtlSec`.

update.title: System upgrade or plugin refresh script
update.description: Use this after a MindAtlas system upgrade, plugin upgrade, or shipped-skill refresh. It reuses existing plugin config by default and only prompts for missing fields.

guide.scriptHighlightsTitle: What the guided scripts do for you
guide.scriptHighlightsDescription: Both scripts are meant to be run on the OpenClaw Gateway host and collapse the usual install or upgrade chores into one flow.

scriptHighlights.prompt: They collect the required plugin config fields directly in the terminal.
scriptHighlights.reuse: The update script reuses the existing MindAtlas plugin config and only asks for fields that are still missing.
scriptHighlights.cleanup: They automatically remove MindAtlas-only legacy `plugins.allow`, `tools.allow`, and empty `tools.profile` compatibility remnants.
scriptHighlights.skills: They back up conflicting old MindAtlas custom skill folders and rerun `configure:skills` for the shipped skills path.
scriptHighlights.restart: They finish by calling `openclaw gateway restart`, then you should validate from a brand-new session.

notes.catalogOnly: OpenClaw only sees catalog items that are currently exposed. Hidden or currently unavailable items should not appear as callable tools, and a session with no visible `mindatlas_*` tools cannot route MindAtlas work automatically.
notes.skillBoundary: The 5 shipped skills tell OpenClaw when it should call MindAtlas and which class of capability to prefer. `mindatlas-overview` is the broad router, `mindatlas-dispatcher` is the dynamic fallback for newly exposed custom capabilities, and summary, retrieval, plus auto-capture are narrower sub-strategies. The actual callable tools still come only from the currently exposed MindAtlas capability catalog.
notes.refresh: After creating, deleting, or editing catalog items, refresh the catalog on the OpenClaw side. If a tool name, exported title, exported description, or input schema changes structurally, active sessions still will not hot-refresh, so start a new session or reload the Gateway or plugin as well. If startup registration fails or a previously unavailable tool becomes available later, fix the issue and reload the Gateway because the plugin no longer late-registers tools after startup. If the current session still shows no MindAtlas tools, the agent should say MindAtlas is not exposed in that session instead of silently substituting generic memory. After plugin or shipped-skill upgrades, prefer the guided `setup:openclaw` or `update:openclaw` scripts before validating again.
